statements.status_notes: GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w: when setuptools installs a wheel through its legacy Wheel.install_as_egg path, entries in the wheel's .dist-info/namespace_packages.txt were split on '.' and passed to os.path.join, so an entry that is an absolute path (a drive-qualified or UNC path on Windows, or an absolute POSIX path) discarded the destination egg directory and created a fixed-content __init__.py at a location chosen by the wheel. It affects setuptools 38.2.2 up to but not including 84.1.0 and is fixed in 84.1.0 by https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/commit/6d07b8d17890dda58d944ac51e58f54af92d52af, which adds _resolve_namespace_dir to validate namespace entries as dotted module names on every platform (https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/security/advisories/GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w, https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/releases/tag/v84.1.0). The advisory describes the Windows form, but the fix commit states that an absolute POSIX path escapes the same way, so Linux builds are treated as affected; the fix commit also notes that this code is reached only through the deprecated setup_requires mechanism when setup() is invoked outside a PEP 517 frontend. Checked setuptools/wheel.py, and the compiled wheel bytecode in the py3.10-setuptools-pyc subpackage, in every py3.10-setuptools package published for Alpine 3.23 by 2026-11-28 (80.9.0-r2, 82.0.0-r0, 82.0.1-r0, 82.0.1-r1, 83.0.0-r0, 84.0.0-r0 and 84.0.0-r1, x86_64 and aarch64). Each ships setuptools/wheel.py byte for byte as in the upstream tag of the setuptools version it carries (v80.9.0, v82.0.0, v82.0.1, v83.0.0 or v84.0.0), with the unvalidated os.path.join of namespace entries and no _resolve_namespace_dir, and none of the bytecode files contains _resolve_namespace_dir. No published build carries the fix, so every build is affected until one with setuptools 84.1.0 or later, or a backport of that commit, is published.

GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w: when setuptools installs a wheel through its legacy Wheel.install_as_egg path in setuptools/wheel.py, entries in the wheel's .dist-info/namespace_packages.txt were passed to os.path.join, so an absolute-path entry could create an __init__.py outside the destination egg directory. It affects setuptools 38.2.2 up to but not including 84.1.0 and is fixed in 84.1.0 by https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/commit/6d07b8d17890dda58d944ac51e58f54af92d52af, which adds _resolve_namespace_dir to validate namespace entries (https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/security/advisories/GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w, https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/releases/tag/v84.1.0). No published build of this owner contains a vulnerable setuptools/wheel.py. We read the md5sums manifests of all 58 airflow packages for Debian 13 published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28, 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-17, amd64 and arm64 (116 package files), which list every file each package installs with its digest, and unpacked the amd64 and arm64 packages of 3.3.0-0, 3.3.2-19, 3.4.0-0 and 3.4.0-17, including the wheels inside them. 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-0 contain no setuptools distribution and no setuptools/wheel.py; babel and cffi ship small setuptools integration modules that import it and do nothing without it. 3.4.0-1 to 3.4.0-17 contain setuptools 84.2.1 twice: installed under /usr/lib/airflow/lib/python3.13/site-packages, with a setuptools/wheel.py byte for byte the file in the PyPI 84.2.1 wheel, and as the setuptools wheel that virtualenv embeds, byte for byte the 84.2.1 wheel on PyPI; that wheel.py defines _resolve_namespace_dir and uses it for namespace entries. The same packages carry the pip 26.2.2 wheel that virtualenv embeds, whose vendored pkg_resources comes from setuptools 70.3.0 (its pip/_vendor/vendor.txt lists setuptools==70.3.0); in the unpacked 3.4.0-17 copy, which has the same digest in every one of those packages, pip vendors only pkg_resources from setuptools, not setuptools/wheel.py or install_as_egg. The range therefore starts the fixed side at the first published build, 3.3.0-0.
